report.summary: Chunk 4 of 4: defines _HEADLESS_EXCERPT_LINES constant, _render helper, and document_skeleton function with fallback logic and DocSkeleton construction.

handoff.purpose: Define _HEADLESS_EXCERPT_LINES, _render, and document_skeleton with multiple degradation rungs.

symbols.name: _HEADLESS_EXCERPT_LINES
symbols.note: Integer constant set to 12; controls number of excerpt lines for headless documents.

symbols.name: _render
symbols.note: Internal function that renders a heading tree (or excerpt) into a formatted string with optional annotations and truncation.

symbols.name: document_skeleton
symbols.note: Public function that produces a DocSkeleton by trying increasingly degraded representations until one fits within a character cap.

claims.text: A document with no headings has no tree to keep, so the outline degenerates to a header and a receipt -- true, and useless to the model reading it. Mirroring slice._skeleton's own fallback for an unparseable file, a bounded head excerpt is emitted instead, and labelled as an excerpt so it is never mistaken for the whole document.
claims.why: The claim references slice._skeleton which is outside this chunk. The excerpt behavior is implemented in _render when heads is empty, but the mirroring claim cannot be verified.

claims.text: HARD INVARIANT, tested: len(result.text) <= len(text), and <= max_chars when one is given.
claims.why: The invariant is stated as tested but no test code is present in this chunk. The code itself ensures len(rendered) <= cap where cap <= len(text), so the invariant holds in this chunk, but the 'tested' part cannot be verified.

claims.text: A distilled view larger than its own source is not a distillation.
claims.why: The code always caps at len(text) and returns a representation that is no larger than the original text (cap <= len(text)).

claims.text: The ladder is fixed and deterministic: 1. heading tree with per-heading provenance; 2. the same tree without annotations; 3. the tree truncated to the first N headings, saying how many were omitted (N halved until it fits, so the outcome is a function of the input, not of a search order); 4. the raw document, with distilled=False.
claims.why: The code tries (degraded='full', annotate=True), then (degraded='no_annotations', annotate=False), then a while loop halving limit, then raw. This matches the described ladder.

claims.text: Every rung says what it dropped. There is no rung that drops silently.
claims.why: Every returned DocSkeleton includes dropped_chars, and the _render function appends a PROSE DROPPED line. The receipt is always included.

observations.what: The _render function's first line of output includes a hardcoded annotation ' (document skeleton: heading tree kept, prose dropped)' which appears in all rendered skeletons.

In _render, when limit is not None and heads length exceeds limit, a line is added indicating omitted headings. This line is counted in kept_lines via len(out) after appending, but the omitted headings themselves are not counted in kept_lines.

In document_skeleton, the cap is set to min(len(text), max_chars) when max_chars is not None, but the raw fallback uses text[:max_chars] directly, which may clip mid-character for multi-byte characters. However, this is consistent with the stated invariant.
